question: When was the Lucknow Pact signed by All India Muslim League and Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1916**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lucknow Pact** was** signed by the All India Muslim League and the Indian National Congress in 1916.**
 
• **The Lucknow Pact was a significant event in the Indian National Movement.**
 
• It marked the reunion of the moderate and extremist factions of the Congress**, which had split in 1907.**
 
• This agreement brought the** Muslim League and the Indian National Congress closer.**
 
• **They agreed to work together to put pressure on the British Government to grant more political power to Indians.**
 
• The pact recognized separate electorates for Muslims in provinces where they were a minority, which was a significant demand of the Muslim League.
 
• The pact was also significant in that it proposed the **idea of granting more autonomy to the provinces, which eventually laid the groundwork for India's federal structure post-independence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Event
 
 
 
 

 1911
 
 
The 26th session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta.

 
It was presided by Bishan Narayan Dar.

 
This session opposed the partition of Bengal.

 
 
 

 1906
 
 
The 21st session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta. Dadabhai Naoroji, one of the founders of the Indian National Congress, presided over it.

 
This session was significant because it adopted 'Swaraj' (Self-rule) as the goal of the Indian National Congress.

 
 
 

 1919
 
 
The Indian National Congress, under the presidency of Motilal Nehru, committed itself to fight for dominion status and the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms were adopted.

 
In response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the Congress initiated widespread protests.
